data.title: Lenovo Leaps 8% To Lead Hong Kong Stocks Higher
data.description:

The Hang Seng TECH Index rose 47.25 points, or 1.16%, to 4,108.24, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index added 24.98 points, or 0.31%, to 8,128.25. The Hang Seng Biotech Index climbed 174.97 points, or 1.19%, to 14,858.25.

Lenovo Group was among the notable movers, rising 8.01% to HK$28.06. Alibaba’s Hong Kong-listed shares gained 2.26% to HK$108.80, while Xiaomi fell 1.55% to HK$26.66.

Tencent’s shares were priced at HK$417.80, while the stock ranked among the market’s highest-turnover counters with HK$7.90 billion traded. Alibaba recorded HK$5.65 billion in turnover, followed by Lenovo at HK$5.04 billion.

Trading on the Main Board reached HK$178.20 billion, while turnover on the Growth Enterprise Market stood at HK$63 million.

Southbound Stock Connect trading recorded turnover of HK$42.31 billion through Shanghai Connect and HK$23.10 billion through Shenzhen Connect.

data.title: Wall Street Slides As AI Financing Fears, Oil Price Surge Rattle Investors
data.description:
Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday as concerns over financing for artificial intelligence infrastructure companies and rising oil prices weighed on sentiment, sending the Nasdaq down 2.19%.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.19% to 26,128.13 points, while the S&P 500 declined 1.22% to 7,649.71 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 0.55% to 51,891.77 points.

AI-related stocks came under renewed pressure amid concerns that heavily indebted infrastructure companies may struggle to generate sufficient profits to service their borrowings, particularly if interest rates remain elevated.

Nvidia-backed data centre operator CoreWeave plunged 12% on Friday, extending its losses over the past five sessions to about 25%. Its bonds also sold off sharply during the week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom fell 3.6%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 2.5%, putting it on track for an eighth consecutive session of losses.

Investors were also rattled by a more than 3% jump in oil prices amid concerns over Middle Eastern supplies, adding to inflation worries following hotter-than-expected US consumer and producer price readings earlier in the week.

“There is some fear in the market,” said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at US Bank Wealth Management.

“High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk.”

Concerns over AI financing also extended to Anthropic, with some existing and prospective investors considering a lower valuation for the company’s upcoming initial public offering, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led by communication services, which fell 2.52%, followed by information technology at 2.38%.

The S&P 500 was heading for its steepest weekly decline since January, while the Nasdaq was on track for its sharpest weekly fall since June.

Investors are also preparing for a busy earnings season next week, with Tesla, Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble among the companies scheduled to report quarterly results. Analysts expect earnings growth of more than 30% on average, driven by major AI-related technology companies, according to LSEG data.

Meanwhile, markets increasingly expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects the central bank to raise rates by 25 basis points in both December and January.

Reuters

data.title: KOSPI Plunges 7.57% After Trading Halt Triggered
data.description:
South Korea’s KOSPI tumbled 7.57% on Oct 15 after a sharp sell-off triggered a temporary trading suspension, with the benchmark closing down 454.59 points at 5,554.22.

Trading in the KOSPI and KOSDAQ markets was suspended for 20 minutes shortly after noon after both indices fell more than 8% from their previous closes, according to a report by The Rio Times carried by UA.News.

A 10-minute auction was held before continuous trading resumed. The KOSDAQ closed at 760.82, down 7.65%.

Under the KOSPI’s circuit-breaker rules, trading is suspended when the index falls at least 8% from its previous close and remains at that level for one minute. Further thresholds are set at declines of 15% and 20%.

During the first- and second-level suspensions, continuous trading is halted and new orders are not accepted, although existing orders may be cancelled. A third-level trigger suspends trading for the rest of the session.

data.title: Stock Today: Sime Darby Rises 0.84% Amid RM150 Million Tax Dispute
data.description:
Sime Darby Bhd shares rose 0.84% in afternoon trading, despite the conglomerate facing additional tax assessments totalling RM150.18 million, including penalties, issued against its wholly-owned subsidiary.

As at 3.48pm, the counter gained two sen to RM2.40 from its last adjusted closing price of RM2.38. The stock opened at RM2.39 and traded between RM2.37 and RM2.42 during the session.

Trading volume stood at 3.40 million shares, with buying volume at 179,400 shares against selling volume of 151,900 shares.

The share price movement came after Sime Darby disclosed on Oct 13 that its subsidiary, Sime Darby Holdings Bhd, was contesting the additional assessments issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).

The notices, received on Sept 30, cover seven years of assessment from 2017 to 2023 and stem from the IRB’s decision to classify interest income generated from the subsidiary’s treasury activities as taxable income under Section 4(c) of the Income Tax Act 1967.

Sime Darby said the subsidiary had consulted its tax and legal advisers and believed it had valid grounds to challenge the assessments.

Sime Darby Holdings intends to appeal the IRB’s decision and initiate legal proceedings to contest the basis and validity of the notices. It has 30 days from Sept 30 to lodge its appeal.

data.title: US Dollar Heads For Weekly Loss As AI Selloff Shifts Rate Outlook
data.description:
The US dollar was on track for its first weekly decline in more than a month against the euro and yen on Friday, as investors assessed the fallout from a selloff in artificial intelligence stocks and expectations for Federal Reserve policy.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six major currencies, fell 0.25% to 101.77 and was set for a 0.45% weekly decline.

AI stocks tumbled this week, with concerns spreading to parts of the credit market as investors questioned whether data centre operators could generate sufficient profits to service their debts.

Analysts said Wednesday’s market movements offered a preview of how currencies could react to a larger AI-driven selloff, with the dollar weakening instead of attracting safe-haven demand as investors reassessed the outlook for US interest rates.

Macquarie Group global foreign exchange and rates strategist Thierry Wizman said a reduction in the outlook for AI investment could weigh on the dollar and US Treasury yields in the coming months and into 2027.

“That’s because it would reduce bond supply and impair US growth, all else equal,” he said.

US Treasury yields fell earlier this week despite hotter-than-expected inflation data, as cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials tempered expectations of an October rate hike. Markets assigned an 87% probability to the Fed keeping rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

The euro rose 0.14% to US$1.1235 after gaining 0.56% on Thursday, its biggest daily increase in two months. It was on track for a 0.39% weekly gain.

The yen was set for a 0.28% weekly rise after four consecutive weeks of losses, trading 0.05% higher at 157.89 per US dollar.

ING foreign exchange strategist Chris Turner said the dollar was likely to consolidate near recent highs unless AI stocks and broader risk assets suffered another sharp decline.

“It is only when short end rates break lower that the dollar is ready to drop. And we are not there yet,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Swiss franc was set for a 0.61% weekly gain against the dollar, supported by its safe-haven status and expectations that Switzerland was unlikely to cut interest rates below zero.

The Australian dollar rose 0.55% to US$0.6959 but remained on track for a 0.3% weekly decline after weaker-than-expected employment data reduced expectations of another interest rate increase.

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Friday that the central bank would continue raising interest rates in line with economic and financial developments.

Higher oil prices tend to support the US dollar while weighing on energy-importing currencies such as the euro and yen. Meanwhile, investors were also watching developments in the Middle East and Ukraine for potential implications for inflation and global growth.

Reuters

data.title: Stock Today: Vestland Gains 1.11% After RM225 Million Kelantan Contract Win

As at 3.23pm, the ACE Market-listed counter gained one sen to 91 sen, from its last adjusted closing price of 90 sen. The stock opened at 91.5 sen and traded between a high of 93.5 sen and a low of 90 sen.

Trading volume stood at 1.35 million shares, with buying interest at 20,000 shares against selling volume of 159,000 shares.

The RM225.07 million contract is scheduled to commence on Oct 28, 2026, with completion targeted for Oct 14, 2028.

The project is expected to provide the group with revenue visibility into 2028, covering river widening, related structures and associated infrastructure works.

data.title: Stock Today: Kelington Eases 0.71% After RM544 Million Sarawak Contract Wins
data.description:
Kelington Group Bhd shares fell 0.71% in afternoon trading on Friday despite securing additional contracts worth RM128 million for an advanced data storage manufacturing facility in Sarawak earlier this week.

At 2.37 pm, the engineering solutions provider was down six sen to RM8.44, giving it a market price below its last adjusted closing price of RM8.50. The stock opened at RM8.55, reached an intraday high of RM8.58 and touched a low of RM8.35.

Trading volume stood at 2.09 million shares, with 1.01 million shares on the buy side and 362,000 shares on the sell side.

On Oct 13, Kelington announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd, had secured an additional RM128 million contract from a manufacturing company operating at the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone in Kuching.

The latest award brought the total value of contracts and purchase orders from the same customer to approximately RM544 million, up from RM416 million previously.

The contract covers the design and construction of ultra-high-purity deionised water generation systems and a wastewater treatment plant for the customer’s facility expansion.

The project is expected to begin immediately and be completed by April 2028. Kelington said the contract would contribute positively to its earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, and subsequent financial periods until completion.

data.title: Heavyweights Drag The FBM KLCI 10.75 Points Lower At Midday

Among the top gainers, ViTrox Corporation Bhd surged 38 sen to RM10.70, followed by Petronas Dagangan Bhd, which rose 28 sen to RM19.48.

Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd and Pekat Group Bhd each gained 22 sen to RM40.62 and RM2.75, respectively, while Pentamaster Corporation Bhd advanced 20 sen to RM5.60.

Zetrix AI Bhd emerged as the most actively traded counter at midday, slipping half a sen to six sen, with approximately 209.74 million shares changing hands.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd added one sen to 91 sen on turnover of 39.65 million shares, while Ni Hsin Group Bhd eased one sen to 41.5 sen, with 29.71 million shares traded.

Trading volume stood at 1.9 billion units valued at RM1.43 billion.

Overall, the midday performance reflected a divergence between weakness in selected blue-chip stocks and continued buying interest in mid-cap and smaller counters, as investors assessed the market’s direction ahead of the afternoon session.

data.title: Gold Holds Near US$4,160 An Ounce As Treasury Yields Fall
data.description:
Gold prices steadied near US$4,160 an oz on Oct 16, after recording their biggest gain in more than two weeks as a global stock market sell-off drove investors towards safe-haven assets.

Bloomberg reported that spot gold slipped 0.3% to US$4,158.03 an oz as of 7.48am, following a 1.6% surge in the previous session, supported by falling US Treasury yields.

The rally came as Wall Street investors shifted away from chipmakers amid growing concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom, triggering a global bond rally.

US Treasury yields fell by as much as 12 to 15 basis points across the curve, boosting demand for non-yielding assets such as gold.

Bullion also recovered losses triggered by stronger-than-expected US inflation data for September, which heightened expectations of a potential Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October.

Investors are now awaiting remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh at an International Monetary Fund meeting in Bangkok for further clues on the central bank’s monetary policy outlook.

Meanwhile, silver declined 0.5% to US$57.13 an oz, while platinum and palladium remained largely unchanged.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was flat after slipping 0.3% in the previous session, as easing pressure on global equities tempered demand for safe-haven assets.

data.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Remain Under Pressure As Crypto Market Faces Volatility
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum traded cautiously on Oct 16, as investors assessed the impact of stronger-than-expected US inflation data, interest rate uncertainty and a broader sell-off in risk-sensitive assets.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, was trading around US$82,259, slipping marginally from US$82,417 at the previous session’s close, according to OKX price data. The digital asset had fallen below US$80,000 on Oct 15 before staging a recovery.

Ethereum also remained under pressure following the sharp decline on Oct 15, when the second-largest cryptocurrency dropped 6.5% to around US$2,353 amid widespread selling across digital assets.

The cryptocurrency market has faced heightened volatility after US inflation figures exceeded expectations, raising concerns that the Federal Reserve could maintain a restrictive monetary policy or increase interest rates.

Selling pressure has also been compounded by weakness in technology stocks, particularly companies linked to artificial intelligence, prompting investors to reduce exposure to speculative assets.

Meanwhile, leveraged cryptocurrency positions faced substantial liquidations, intensifying price fluctuations as traders unwound bullish bets.

Market participants are closely monitoring Bitcoin’s ability to hold above US$80,000, while Ethereum’s performance around the US$2,400 level remains a key focus.

With uncertainty surrounding US monetary policy and global risk sentiment, both cryptocurrencies could face further volatility in the near term.

data.title: Kospi Rebounds 2.53% After ‘Black Thursday’ Rout, Chip Stocks Recover
data.description:
South Korean shares rebounded on Friday after plunging more than 7 per cent in the previous session, with heavyweight semiconductor stocks recovering as investors returned to the market for bargains, per bloomingbit.

As of 9.57 am, the benchmark Kospi had risen 140.26 points, or 2.53 per cent, to 5,694.48, after opening 1.80 per cent higher at 5,653.99. The index climbed to an intraday high of 5,699.83, approaching the 5,700 level.

Individual investors were net buyers of 116.5 billion won while institutional investors purchased 144.9 billion won. Foreign investors, however, remained net sellers, offloading 361.9 billion won worth of shares.

Semiconductor heavyweights led the recovery, with Samsung Electronics gaining 2.14 per cent to 214,500 won and SK Hynix rising 2.30 per cent to 1.291 million won. Hyundai Motor advanced 5.25 per cent, Samsung Electro-Mechanics added 3.18 per cent and SK Square climbed 3.01 per cent.

The tech-heavy Kosdaq index also rallied, gaining 27.92 points, or 3.67 per cent, to 788.74.

The rebound followed Thursday’s sharp sell-off, when the Kospi tumbled 454.59 points, or 7.57 per cent, to 5,554.22, triggering a circuit breaker that briefly halted trading. Concerns over persistent US inflation, the prospect of tighter monetary policy and questions surrounding the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending weighed on sentiment.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged 9.48 per cent and 11.06 per cent, respectively, during the previous session.

Overnight gains on Wall Street and falling US Treasury yields helped support the recovery. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.08 per cent, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite gained 0.33 per cent and 0.08 per cent, respectively.

Despite Friday’s rebound, continued foreign selling suggested that investor confidence remained fragile following the previous day’s sharp losses.

data.title: Ringgit Opens Flat Ahead Of Malaysia GDP Estimate
data.description:
The ringgit opened little changed against the US dollar on Friday as expectations of continued restrictive US monetary policy offset support from a weaker greenback, with investors also awaiting Malaysia’s third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) estimate.

At 8 am, the ringgit stood at 4.0800/0845 against the US dollar, compared with Thursday’s close of 4.0800/0835.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.53 per cent to 102.005 points, while Brent crude oil prices declined to around US$105 per barrel. A weaker dollar would typically support the ringgit by easing upward pressure on the US currency.

However, persistent US inflationary pressures and expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) would maintain its restrictive monetary stance could limit the local currency’s gains.

Mohd Afzanizam said the International Energy Agency’s pledge to release 100 million barrels of oil from its reserves had temporarily calmed oil markets, although supply disruptions remained unresolved. Meanwhile, concerns over valuations of artificial intelligence-related stocks prompted a flight to safety, driving US Treasury yields lower.

“Still, the latest print on the US Producer Price Index (PPI) reading for September suggested that the inflation rate remains elevated, with the index rising 6.3 per cent, exceeding the consensus forecast of 5.3 per cent. This could mean the Fed is likely to maintain its restrictive posture at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting at the end of this month,” he told Bernama.

Domestically, investors are awaiting Malaysia’s advance estimate of third-quarter GDP growth, due today.

Mohd Afzanizam expects the provisional figure to reach around 5.2 per cent, slower than the 6.0 per cent growth recorded in the second quarter but still above the economy’s trend growth level.

He added that expectations of a normalisation of the overnight policy rate could provide support to the ringgit.

He expects the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.09 today.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5797/5827 from 2.5869/5892 at Thursday’s close and rose against the euro to 4.5741/5791 from 4.5761/5801. However, it weakened against the British pound to 4.4138/4197 from 4.4101/4147.

Against regional currencies, the ringgit was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 227.4/227.8 and remained steady against the Philippine peso at 6.47/6.48. It slipped marginally against the Singapore dollar to 3.1820/1858 from 3.1818/1848 but strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1675/1889 from 12.1758/1914.

data.title: HSIF Short Position Maintained With 24,000-Point Support In Focus
data.description:

However, a bullish reversal candlestick could signal a recovery towards the 20-day simple moving average (SMA), although the research house said the bearish technical setup remained intact.

Resistance levels are pegged at 25,000 points and 25,600 points, while support remains at 24,000 points and 23,600 points.

data.title: Wall Street Closes Higher With Investors Rotating Away From AI Stocks
data.description:
Wall Street ended higher on Thursday as investors shifted towards healthcare and consumer stocks amid renewed concerns over artificial intelligence-related valuations, rising borrowing costs and persistent inflation.

The S&P 500 gained 0.33% to close at 7,744.06 points, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.08% to 26,713.03 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed, rising 1.08% to 52,177.69 points.

Healthcare stocks led the S&P 500’s sector gains, advancing 1.84%, followed by materials, which rose 1.71%. Eli Lilly gained more than 3%, UnitedHealth Group climbed 2.8% and Walmart added 1.4% after Deutsche Bank upgraded its ratings on the companies.

Technology shares remained under pressure, with Nvidia falling 1.8% after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) struck a cautious tone on its 2027 outlook despite reporting its sixth consecutive record quarterly profit. Dell Technologies dropped 6.9% while Hewlett Packard Enterprise declined 7.1%, extending losses from the previous session amid concerns over AI companies’ exposure to higher borrowing costs.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 0.9%, marking its seventh consecutive session of losses.

“The cost to finance everything, whether it be a new single-family house or a giant data centre, is going up, and that has implications for lots of stuff in the stock market,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management.

Inflation concerns also weighed on sentiment after US producer prices recorded their largest increase in four-and-a-half years in September. Hotter-than-expected consumer inflation data a day earlier had fuelled expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Interest rate traders were pricing in a 67% chance of a rate increase by December, up from 62% on Wednesday, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

Despite Thursday’s gains, the S&P 500 remained under pressure from the technology sector’s recent weakness. The index was still up about 13% in 2026, with much of its advance driven by AI-related stocks.

Trading volume was heavy, with 20.7 billion shares changing hands on US exchanges, compared with the average of 17.6 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.
